title: Former Product Lead at Palantir Technologies Discusses Evolution and Strategic Role of Forward Deployed Engineering Teams
expert: Former Product Lead and FDE Lead at Palantir (13 years); now CTO and co-founder of an FDE consultancy doing outsourced FDE work for Palantir customers
verdict: A 13-year Palantir FDE lead, now running a partner consultancy, says Palantir is handing long-term implementation to partners as customers are priced out at a few million dollars per FDE a year.

Delivery capacity: 🟡 **Long-term implementation moving to partners; customers "priced out" at a few million dollars per FDE per year** (estimate); consistent with Cleveland SI checks that customers complain Palantir leaves after initial deployment (SB #62491). → Tenet 5 (delivery capacity) →
🔴 **FDE resources not guaranteed under consumption-based contracts**, risking friction on complex implementations; first read. → Tenet 5 (delivery capacity) ↓
Adj OM vs 60%: 🟢 **Consumption pricing decouples platform revenue from FDE headcount**; first read. → Tenet 3 (adj OM ≥60%) ↑

changes: Partner share of delivery: Palantir handing long-term work to partners vs Cleveland SI checks of Palantir practices growing ~3x and ~7x (SB #62489, 2026-10-29) and customers complaining Palantir leaves after initial deployment (SB #62491, 2026-10-29): **consistent**.

Entry cost: a few million dollars per FDE per year vs an ex-Palantir sales exec saying mid-market won't accept US$1.5m-plus to get started (SB #64789, 2026-09-05): **consistent** (high cost limits mid-market).
thesis_impact: Tenet 5 (delivery capacity): → — partners absorb long-term delivery, but FDE support is no longer guaranteed under consumption contracts.
Tenet 3 (adj OM ≥60%): ↑ — consumption pricing scales revenue without FDE headcount.
Tenet 1 (US commercial growth): ↓ slight — a few million dollars per FDE prices out smaller customers.
